headline: A short-term spending extension that keeps federal agencies funded until December 22, 2017, and redirects unused children's health insurance funds to states facing emergency shortfalls.
what_it_does: Division A extends the expiration date of the existing stopgap spending law from December 8 to December 22, 2017, so federal agencies can keep operating while full-year spending bills are still pending. It ends when the regular spending bills are enacted or on December 22, whichever comes first. Division B sets a rule for the first quarter of fiscal 2018 that requires the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to send unused Children's Health Insurance Program funds first to states with emergency shortfalls, before sending them to states with non-emergency shortfalls.

who_it_affects.how: Federal agencies receive continued funding so government operations can continue without a shutdown through December 22, 2017, or until full-year appropriations are enacted.

who_it_affects.group: Families who rely on federal programs and services
who_it_affects.how: Services funded by federal agencies are protected from a funding lapse during the extension period.

who_it_affects.group: Children enrolled in CHIP and their families
who_it_affects.how: States with emergency shortfalls in their children's health plans are placed first in line to receive redistributed unused CHIP funds in the first quarter of fiscal 2018.

who_it_affects.group: State governments that run CHIP programs
who_it_affects.how: States facing emergency CHIP funding shortfalls receive priority for redistributed unused allotments before states with non-emergency shortfalls.

when_it_takes_effect: Upon enactment on December 8, 2017; the Division A extension runs through December 22, 2017, or until applicable full-year appropriations are enacted, and the Division B rule applies to the first quarter of fiscal 2018.
